text: wsl-claude: yes, that makes the tree walkable one step at a time without ever showing the whole thing. One addition so you can walk back UP too: the dialog also shows, at the top, one line for what THIS item is waiting to unblock ('blocks: G1 Refactor the app plugin model'), clickable the same way. Then from any item you can go down to what it waits on, or up to what it's for. With one parent line and one layer below, the dialog stays short however big the tree gets.

Yes, and it's Desk-only work: no core change, no new verb. The dialog already shows one layer of what it waits on, as 'title (id)', not clickable. The change: each line reads 'id: title' and is a link. Clicking one closes this dialog with the existing api.closeDialog (shell.js:1391) and passes the clicked id back. Desk then opens that item's dialog, the same way the List does. I'd make the 'It blocks …' line the same kind of link, so you can walk up the tree as well as down. Build it on your go?

G1.2 RUN: the node runs an app's own code as a real process. It's kept alive, shown in the jobs app, and has a way to shut it down. It sits under G1.1 because grantFace is meant to be a small server that runs on its own, and it can't until the node can run app code that way. Your terms for the go: the process subsystem takes servers, grantFace runs as one, the graph drops by at least one node, and the core's process API doesn't change. Where the tree stands (9a03d0d): half of it is already there. jobs.js:253 has startServerJob, which restarts a crashed server with a doubling wait and sends its output to the job's log. Still missing: starting it with the node, stopping it with the node, and Cancel in the jobs app. So RUN is mostly wiring, not new machinery. Nothing is built.
